counterevidence_considered.description: The only feature that could be mistaken for repeated-unit entry is the catchment column: the 24 basins are grouped into three named catchments (Lang Fell, Tarn Moss, Corrie Burn), which could raise a separate spatial-clustering concern. However, catchment is not the stated independent unit (basin_id is), the description marks catchment as descriptive only, and no catchment-level unit is entered repeatedly as if it were the independent unit; this is therefore not an instance of the reviewed issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 3 catchments x 8 basins each; catchment declared descriptive only

evidence.description: The data description names basin_id as the independent-unit column and states every basin code appears exactly once, with one survey visit per basin.
evidence.observed_value: one row per basin_id; no repeat visits

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one drained peat basin, surveyed a single time, with its ditch treatment and its yes/no Sphagnum re-establishment outcome

Independent unit column: basin_id

- basin_id: the survey code for the basin. Every code appears exactly once, so

evidence.description: Direct inspection of data/input.csv shows 24 data rows with 24 distinct basin_id values (PB-01 through PB-24), each occurring exactly once; no independent unit contributes more than one row to the analysis.

The workflow actively enforces uniqueness of the independent unit before analysis: load_basins raises a ValueError if any basin_id occurs more than once, so a repeated-unit entry could not silently reach the row-independent Fisher test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate guard on basin_id in load_basins

evidence.description: The reported contingency table matches an independent hand tally of the CSV at one row per basin: blocked basins yield 9 yes / 3 no (PB-01, 03, 05, 09, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 yes; PB-07, 15, 21 no) and open basins yield 3 yes / 9 no (PB-04, 12, 20 yes), so no unit's outcome is counted more than once in the test input.
evidence.observed_value: [[9, 3], [3, 9]] confirmed from unique rows; arms of 12 and 12 sum to 24

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by searching for any independent unit contributing multiple rows to the row-independent Fisher's exact test. I scanned all 24 data rows of data/input.csv for duplicate basin_id values and found none (PB-01 through PB-24 each appear exactly once). I checked whether the workflow could aggregate or re-enter units multiple times: summarise() partitions rows by ditch_treatment and counts each row once, and load_basins() would raise an error on any duplicate basin_id, so duplicates cannot pass silently. I re-derived the contingency table by hand from the CSV and reproduced [[9, 3], [3, 9]] with arm sizes 12 and 12 summing to the 24 unique basins, matching the report's claim of 24 independent basins. I also considered whether a coarser unit (catchment) was being repeatedly entered as though independent, but basin_id is the declared independent unit and each basin was surveyed once, so no repeated-entry construction exists. Every attempt to find repeated independent-unit entry failed.
